Kakinada: The landfall process of Cyclone ‘Arnab’ is underway along the Andhra Pradesh coast, bringing torrential rainfall and destructive winds that have severely disrupted normal life in several coastal districts.
The cyclonic storm began crossing the coast at around 1.10 am on Wednesday (October 28), earlier than initially anticipated.

According to the India Meteorological Department […] The post Cyclone Arnab Landfall Underway in Andhra Pradesh, Winds May Reach 140 kmph; Heavy Rain Lashes Coastal Districts, Watch appeared first on KalingaTV.

Cyclone Arnab remained "practically stationary" along the Andhra Pradesh coast early on Wednesday and the landfall process is expected to continue for the next 2-3 hours, the IMD said, as heavy rains lashed a number of districts in the southern state.
At some places in the state, police rescued stranded people.
Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu reviewed the situation on Wednesday morning.
According to the IMD, the northern spiral band of the cyclone has further entered the land, while the storm's centre remains very close to the coastline.

"The cyclone remains practically stationary along the Andhra Pradesh coast, and the landfall process is expected to continue for another 2-3 hours," the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in an update at 5.30 am.
More than 84,000 people were moved to shelters as authorities prioritised saving lives and maintaining emergency services.

article_sentences: Cyclone Arnab's landfall continued along the Andhra Pradesh coast as police rescued stranded residents.
Heavy rainfall, flooding and winds gusting to 150 kmph disrupted several coastal districts.

The landfall process of very severe cyclonic storm Arnab continued along the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday, with the storm's centre remaining close to the coastline, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.
The northern spiral band of the cyclone had moved further inland, and the landfall process was expected to continue for another three hours.
At least 91 trains and 21 flights were cancelled on Tuesday and Wednesday as authorities stepped up precautionary measures ahead of the cyclone.
The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) said 84,396 people had been evacuated to shelters across the state.
The IMD said the cyclone was located over the west-central Bay of Bengal, near latitude 16.4 degrees north and longitude 82.0 degrees east.
Its centre was around 30 km east of Narsapur, 45 km south-southwest of Yanam, 70 km south-southwest of Kakinada and 90 km east-northeast of Machilipatnam.
India Today correspondent Apoorva Jayachandran was in Kakinada to bring you the updates.
The storm was expected to move northwestwards and cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to the south of Yanam.
Maximum sustained wind speeds of up to 135 kmph, with gusts reaching 150 kmph, were forecast during the next three hours.
Heavy rainfall and strong winds battered several parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kakinada and Konaseema districts.

stories.headline: India jewellers hold off gold buying
stories.title: India jewellers hold off gold buying
stories.summary: Indian jewelers are holding back gold purchases ahead of their busiest demand season, betting that a recent drop in prices has further to run, according to the country’s biggest precious metals refiner. Large jewelry chains that typically account for the bulk of sales have yet to fully return to the market, said Samit Guha, chief executive officer and managing director of MMTC-PAMP India Pvt., a joint venture of state-owned MMTC Ltd. and Swiss refinery PAMP SA. Buying has instead been led by small- and mid-sized jewelers, some of which have placed repeat orders, he said. Gold fell below $4,000 an ounce last week for the first time since July, extending its decline to about 24% since the US-Iran war began in late February. Prices had surged past $5,400 to a record in January.Read more - India’s record bank cash surplus fades as RBI curbs rupee betsBigger jewelry makers typically step up purchases when prices start rising to lock in supplies before they become more expensive, while drawing down inventories when they expect further declines, Guha said.Demand in the world’s second-biggest gold consumer has remained subdued this year after the government more than doubled the import duty to 15% in May. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has also repeatedly urged Indians to curb purchases to contain a widening trade deficit. The South Asian nation imports nearly all the gold it consumes. The higher tariff has also pushed more buying into under-the-counter cash markets.“The increase in duty has impacted purchases for us,” Guha said.The caution contrasts with China, the world’s biggest gold consumer, where household demand has picked up recently as prices declined. India’s reluctance to buy adds to signs of weakness just as demand enters its strongest period, with purchases typically concentrated between October and December around Diwali, which falls on November 8 this year.Tighter import rules and weaker rural demand following El Niño-driven monsoon disruptions are expected to curb India’s gold imports, according to Citi Research. Shipments may total about 106 tons from October through December, roughly half the historical fourth-quarter average of 212 tons, it said.MMTC-PAMP’s gold sales are running below last year’s levels, with demand skewed toward smaller coins and bars, Guha said. September sales were roughly flat from a year earlier, while buying has picked up a little in October.“If gold rebounds, we will see buying,” he said.

stories.headline: 4 ministers, 4 political journeys
stories.title: 4 ministers, 4 political journeys
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 27: From decades of electoral experience and party organisation to hard-fought constituency battles, Ali Mohammad Sagar, Saifullah Mir, Shamim Firdous, and Altaf Ahmad Wani (Kaloo) bring distinct political journeys to Chief Minister Omar Abdullah’s expanded cabinet. The four National Conference (NC) leaders represent different constituencies and generations of political contests, with experience spanning legislative service, ministerial responsibilities, and grassroots representation. As they take charge of their new portfolios, their political backgrounds offer a glimpse into the experience and electoral mandates they bring to the government’s developmental agenda. Ali Mohammad Sagar Ali Mohammad Sagar is a senior National Conference (NC) leader and seven-time legislator from Srinagar’s Khanyar assembly constituency. Sagar has built his political career through repeated electoral victories, organisational responsibilities within the NC, and ministerial service in previous National Conference (NC) led governments. His return to the cabinet marks another chapter in his decades-long political career. Sagar did his LLB from the University of Kashmir. His legal education preceded a political career spanning more than four decades. Sagar’s electoral journey began in 1983, when he was first elected to the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly from Khanyar. He subsequently won from the constituency in 1987, 1996, 2002, 2008, and 2014, before securing another victory in the 2024 Assembly election. His electoral record spans several distinct periods in J&K’s political history, with Khanyar remaining the centre of his legislative career. The 2024 Assembly election reaffirmed his position as the NC’s representative from the Srinagar constituency. Sagar received 14,906 votes, defeating independent candidate Sheikh Imran, who polled 4994 votes, by a margin of 9912 votes. Sagar has held senior organisational responsibilities in the NC and is often referred to as the party’s “crisis manager”. In June 2014, he was appointed the party’s General Secretary, succeeding Sheikh Nazir, who had held the position since 1996. Sagar previously served in the NC led government holding the portfolios of Works and Rural Development and Panchayati Raj. Saifullah Mir Saifullah Mir, a senior National Conference (NC) leader, represents the Trehgam assembly constituency of north Kashmir’s Kupwara district. A four-time MLA, Mir has previously represented the neighbouringKupwara constituency for three terms. A lawyer by profession and a former minister in the Jammu and Kashmir government, Mir returned to the Legislative Assembly in 2024 after winning the newly delineated Trehgam seat. He was continuously elected thrice from the Kupwara assembly constituency in 1996, 2002, and 2008 as an NC candidate. Following the delimitation of assembly constituencies, Mir contested the 2024 election from Trehgam and secured his fourth assembly victory. In the 2024 assembly elections, he won the Trehgam constituency, polling 18,002 votes, defeating People’s Conference (PC) candidate Bashir Ahmad Dar, who polled 14,376 votes, by a margin of 3626 votes. Mir did his LLB from the University of Kashmir in 1987. He previously also served in the NC-led government headed by Omar Abdullah. Mir was inducted into the ministry during a cabinet reshuffle in January 2013, alongside several other NC legislators. Shamim Firdous Shamim Firdous is a senior National Conference (NC) leader and a three-time Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) from HabbaKadal constituency in central Kashmir’s Srinagar district. She won the HabbaKadal assembly seat in 2008 and retained it in the 2014 and 2024 assembly elections. Firdous also chaired the Jammu and Kashmir State Commission for Women, holding the status of a Minister of State. She did her BA and LLB with Honours from the University of Kashmir in 1983. In the 2024 assembly election, Firdous secured 12,437 votes, defeating Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) candidate Ashok Kumar Bhat, who received 2899 votes, winning by a margin of 9538 votes. Beyond her legislative career, Firdous has held responsibilities within the NC Women’s Wing. Altaf Ahmad Wani Altaf Ahmad Wani (Kaloo) is a National Conference (NC) leader who represents the Pahalgam assembly constituency of south Kashmir’s Anantnag district. His political career is marked by an unsuccessful assembly election bid in the 2008 assembly elections, nomination in 2009 to the Legislative Council, and victories in the 2014 and 2024 Assembly elections. His electoral defeats and wins have featured repeated contests against a political heavyweight, Rafi Ahmed Mir, in Pahalgam. Wani won his first Assembly election in 2014, defeating Mir by a narrow margin of 904 votes in a closely contested Pahalgam race. He secured 25,232 votes, while Mir, the PDP candidate, received 24,328 votes. The result reversed the outcome of the 2008 election, when Mir had defeated Wani in Pahalgam. The two politicians would face each other again in the 2024 Assembly elections, making their electoral rivalry a recurring feature of Pahalgam’s political contest. In the 2024 assembly elections, Wani defeated Mir by a substantially larger margin of 13,756 votes, polling 26,210 votes, while Mir, contesting on the Apni Party ticket, received 12,454 votes. Wani did his Engineering in Mechanical Engineering from Islamia Institute of Technology, Bangalore, in 1995.
